newsitem.title: DUBAI: U.S. pays $32.5 mln to Airbus shoot-down victims.
newsitem.headline: U.S. pays $32.5 mln to Airbus shoot-down victims.

text.p: The United States has paid some $32.5 million in compensation over the shooting down of an Iranian airliner in 1988 by a U.S. warship which killed 290 people, an Iranian newspaper said on Wednesday.

The daily Salam quoted Goodarz Eftekhar Jahromi, the top Iranian official in charge of dealing with Iran's claims over the shoot-down, as saying that so far 143 families of victims had been paid 32.5 million through a Swiss bank account and the Swiss Embassy which represents U.S. interests in Iran.
He said 216 families of victims had submitted compensation applications in the past year and the remaining claims were being handled.
Washington said the ship's crew mistook the airliner for an attacking Iranian fighter plane. Tehran said the attack was deliberate.

The incident near the Strait of Hormuz at the mouth of the Gulf occurred when Iranian and U.S. forces were engaged in one of their several clashes in the latter stages of the eight-year Iran-Iraq war which ended with a ceasefire in August 1988.
In February 1996 the U.S. State Department announced a $131.8 million settlement between the two deeply hostile countries.

Washington said it would pay $300,000 for each wage-earning victim and $150,000 for each victim who was not earning wages. The funds would go to the families of each of the 248 Iranians who were among the Airbus passengers. The State Department said no money would be paid to the Iranian government.
The United States has already compensated families of non-Iranian victims of the incident.

All 290 people on board the Iran Air Airbus A300, flying from the Iranian port of Bandar Abbas to Dubai in the United Arab Emirates across the Gulf, were killed when the U.S. cruiser Vincennes shot it down on July 3, 1988.
